title: Asia‐enriched survey of spatial biology and three‐dimensional pathology
abstract: An Asia-enriched survey of 239 respondents found that reported implementation of spatial biology and three-dimensional pathology varied across self-rated experience groups. Respondents identified cost, analytical complexity, limited standardization, and insufficient interdisciplinary expertise as barriers, highlighting the needs for practical workflows and computational support.

title: Hepatic sinusoidal obstruction syndrome and the search for a modifiable endothelial state
abstract: Pyrrolizidine alkaloid (PA) exposure, haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), and repeated oxaliplatin treatment provide distinct contexts for sinusoidal endothelial injury, with differing mechanisms and courses. Oxaliplatin-associated abnormalities may resolve or persist. Illustrated features are conceptual, not validated clinical stages or a shared temporal sequence. Recognition varies by setting and age; the proposed gap remains unvalidated. Current biomarkers and imaging do not establish the reversibility of liver sinusoidal endothelial cell (LSEC) injury. Clinical care remains etiology-specific. Testing whether an endothelial profile can guide treatment selection requires endothelial-associated measures, independent vascular assessment, and prospective evidence of differential treatment benefit. No endothelial-state-based treatment threshold has been validated.

title: iMeta: Biology and medicine in informatics and MetaOmics era
abstract: This study presents a decade-long bibliometric map of informatics and metaomics research in biology and medicine, spanning life and agricultural sciences, basic and translational medicine, methodology innovation, and interdisciplinary frontiers. Aligning these findings with insights from the iMeta Conference 2026, which fostered talent cultivation and academic exchange among global researchers, we further highlight how the iMeta journal community captures the challenges and opportunities in this rapidly evolving era.

title: Urban avian viromes reveal viral diversity of potential public health relevance across China
abstract: Urbanization reshapes ecological interactions at the human-animal interface, yet how it structures viral diversity in urban avian communities remains unclear. Here, we present a pan-urban viromic analysis of avian samples collected across 22 cities in China. We identified 52,314 viral operational taxonomic units, broadly representing species-level viral clusters, revealing extensive and previously underexplored viral diversity. Viral richness varied markedly among cities, largely reflecting variation in bacteriophage diversity, whereas vertebrate-associated viruses showed a comparatively narrower diversity range. Network analyses revealed pronounced geographic structuring of avian viromes, with several cities sharing viral lineages with multiple other cities and acting as hubs of virome connectivity, linked by a core set of widely distributed viral families alongside substantial local heterogeneity. Sequence similarity and phylogenetic analyses showed that 63.1% (2994/4746) of vertebrate-associated viral sequences shared less than 80% similarity with their closest known references, including 65.6% (2718/4143) of DNA virus sequences and 45.8% (276/603) of RNA virus sequences, highlighting pervasive viral novelty across genome types. Further comparisons with reference sequences identified candidate associations with diverse annotated host taxa, including mammals and humans. Functional profiling of auxiliary metabolic genes revealed a highly skewed repertoire dominated by CysH (phosphoadenosine phosphosulfate reductase), a key enzyme in assimilatory sulfate reduction, suggesting that phages may modulate sulfur assimilation in infected bacterial hosts and potentially influence sulfur metabolism in urban bird-associated microbial communities. Together, these findings provide a nationwide view of the spatial organization, evolutionary diversity, and cross-host association patterns of viruses in urban birds, highlighting their role in shaping viral ecology in human-dominated environments.

title: A decade‐scale audit of microbiome AI‐readiness
abstract: A systematic, PRISMA-guided review led by our consortium screened 23,781 human microbiome papers and procured 2896 studies published from 2012 to 2025 that were then scored by reviewers into four Biological Host-Associated AI-Ready Metadata (BHAM) tiers. Only 5.9% of studies deposited sequence data with per-sample host disease status, age, and sex, and 63.1% shared no reusable sequence data, so that 85.5% of roughly 720,000 samples cannot be reused for cross-cohort or artificial intelligence (AI) analyses without contacting the authors. Sequence deposition improved modestly over time, whereas per-sample annotation did not. Journals, repositories, and researchers should require structured, machine-readable metadata at submission, supported by AI-assisted curation.

title: High‐risk Klebsiella pneumoniae shows hospital‐centered genomic connectivity with divergent sublineage dissemination
abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is widespread across human, animal and environmental niches, but whether high‐risk lineages circulate extensively between these reservoirs remains unclear. Here we investigated the ecological distribution and genomic connectivity of K. pneumoniae through four‐season surveillance of hospital, community and farm settings across five Chinese provinces. Whole‐genome sequencing of 902 isolates, including 521 recovered from 3151 non‐clinical samples and 381 from patients, revealed a marked ecological contrast: classical populations predominated in communities and farms, whereas 95.5% of isolates classified as carbapenem‐resistant or hypervirulent originated from hospitals. Genomic analysis identified 2795 closely related isolate pairs and 169 putative transmission events, predominantly within or between hospitals (82.8%). Only 10 events connected different epidemiological settings, frequently involving aquatic environments. Carbapenem‐resistant populations also exhibited genomic links spanning multiple sampling seasons. These patterns were largely driven by ST11, whose major sublineages showed contrasting distributions: ST11‐KL64 formed small, geographically dispersed clusters with occasional cross‐setting links, whereas ST11‐KL25 formed three hospital‐associated clusters accounting for 64.3% of all closely related isolate pairs. Together, our findings reveal a marked distinction between widespread ecological occurrence and predominantly hospital‐centered genomic connectivity of high‐risk K. pneumoniae , highlighting lineage‐specific patterns of dissemination across interconnected ecological settings.

title: Strain level variation in pathogenic invaders alters rhizosphere communities
abstract: Phytopathogen invasion disrupts resident microbiota, and strain-level provides valuable insights in the underlying mechanisms. Here, we first conducted a meta-analysis encompassing bacterial, fungal, and nematode pathogens, revealing a general pattern of changes in resident microbial communities following pathogen invasion. We then examined differences in community responses among strains through inoculation experiments using 30 strains of the bacterial phytopathogen Ralstonia solanacearum. We characterized these strains at physiological(10 response traits) and phenotypical level (41 resource-utilization traits). Functional variation explained 67.9% in resident microbial community responses following invasion, with resource-utilization traits being the best predictors. Moreover, greater trait dissimilarity among strains was associated with greater differences in community responses and deterministic assembly, whereas the relationship between assembly differences and community dissimilarity weakened as trait dissimilarity increased. These findings highlight that intraspecific variation modulates pathogen interaction with the plant microbiome pointing at precision plant disease management strategies.
